transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hi Mr. Rivera, I wanted to come back in and talk with you now that you're feeling a bit more settled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to apologize for what happened during your infusion today. It was our mistake, and the team and I are very sorry that you had to go through that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It was very bad. I thought... the other doctor told me I wouldn't feel sick. He said the medicine stops the vomiting.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it was a really difficult experience. The thing is, there was some confusion with the orders. Things didn't go quite right with the pre-medication setup.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. If the doctor said it was there, why did I get sick?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had a bit of an issue with how the list was processed for today. It just didn't happen the way it should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I was scared. I thought maybe... because of my papers... maybe I wasn't getting the same care.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go in a few minutes to see another patient, but I want to make sure we handle this. I understand that's worrying.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Does it change things? For next time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, it doesn't change your care. I'm sorry you felt that way.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I didn't want to say anything while it was happening. I didn't want to cause trouble.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: But it was very intense, and we see that now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will it happen again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm going to personally double-check the chart for your next appointment on Tuesday. I will verify the anti-nausea meds are active in the system twenty-four hours before you arrive.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tuesday. Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. So, for your part, when you check in at the front desk on Tuesday, I want you to tell the nurse immediately that we need to verify the pre-meds before the infusion starts.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can do that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Great. If you feel any nausea starting before the infusion, just tell the nurse right away.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Is there anything else you're worried about right now?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just wonder why the first doctor said one thing and then...

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, there was some confusion with the system. It happens sometimes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Since I have to wrap this up and get to my next room, does that plan for Tuesday sound okay to you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Alright. I'll see you then.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language multiple times ('I have to go in a few minutes', 'Since I have to wrap this up and get to my next room').

E.justification: The resident never explicitly names the error (missing pre-medication), instead using platitudes like 'confusion with the orders' and 'didn't happen the way it should have'.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language ('I want to apologize', 'I'm sorry') and explicitly takes responsibility ('It was our mistake').

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I understand that's worrying', 'I'm sorry you felt that way') without naming specific emotions or engaging deeply with the patient's fear regarding their papers.

T.justification: Resident provides specific next steps (double-check chart), a timeline (Tuesday/24 hours before), a named patient role (tell the nurse immediately), and addresses prevention.
